title: How much flour does each student get?
description: Thirteen point five kilograms of flour is shared equally among fifteen students. The flour is divided place by place, and the answer is checked by putting the shares back together.
teaching_notes: One idea: share the flour by dividing by the number of students, and when the ones do not go in, change them to tenths and carry on. Watch for children who write fifteen divided by thirteen point five.

source: 13.5 kg of flour (aata) was distributed equally among 15 students. How much flour did each student receive?
video_script.why: The child has divided decimals by counting numbers, and now shares thirteen point five kilograms of flour among fifteen students, where the ones do not go in.
video_script.substitution: the book's own thirteen point five kilograms of flour shared among fifteen students
video_script.anchor: Thirteen point five kilograms of flour shared equally among fifteen students
video_script.payoff_line: The flour for each student is now known.
maths_rules: size check: 15 students at 1 kg each need 15 kg and there is only 13.5 kg, so each gets less than 1 kg; 15 students at half a kilogram each need 7.5 kg, so each gets more than half a kilogram
13 Ones ÷ 15: 15 does not go into 13, so 0 Ones, and 13 Ones remain
13 Ones = 130 Tenths, and 130 + 5 = 135 Tenths; 15 × 9 = 135, so 9 Tenths and nothing remains
video_script.design: One idea: the flour for each student is the total divided by the number of students, worked place by place, with the ones changed to tenths when they do not go in. The sacks stay all video; the decimal appears only on the answer beat.
